title: Bun Bo Hue
subtitle: spicy Vietnamese beef and pork noodle soup from Hue
excerpt: Bun bo Hue is a deeply spiced Vietnamese noodle soup from the old imperial city of Hue. It is richer and spicier than pho, with lemongrass and shrimp paste in the broth. The round rice noodles, braised beef, and pork hock make it one of the most complex and rewarding soups in Vietnamese cooking.
sourceNotes: Bun bo Hue originates from Hue, the former imperial capital of Vietnam. The city is known for its refined and complex cuisine. The soup is spicier and more intensely flavoured than Hanoi pho. It is particularly associated with the Tet lunar new year, when it is served at family gatherings. It is less known internationally than pho but considered by many Vietnamese to be its equal.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The broth can be made a day ahead and improves with time. Reheat to boiling before serving.

content.text: Bun bo Hue is a bigger commitment than pho -- the broth needs at least 2 hours and the aromatics are more complex. The lemongrass must be well bruised before it goes in. Shrimp paste gives the broth its characteristic depth and orange colour. If you cannot find it, the soup is still good without it, but it will taste different.

items.prepNote: cut into large chunks -- or use a pork hock if available
use 2 lemongrass stalks -- bruised and cut into lengths
use 400g round rice noodles (bun) -- or thick rice noodles
halved and lightly charred under a grill
use 1 tbsp shrimp paste if available -- fry briefly in oil then add to broth

content.text: Char the shallots under a hot grill or directly over a flame until lightly blackened. Set aside.
Place the beef and pork in a large saucepan with the cold stock. Bring to a boil. Skim the foam carefully. Reduce to a simmer.
Add the charred shallots, lemongrass, fish sauce, and chilli flakes. Simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is very tender.
Remove the meat. Slice the beef thinly. Pull the pork into chunks. Strain the broth through a fine sieve.
Cook the noodles according to the packet. Drain and divide between deep bowls.
Top with beef, pork, and spring onion. Ladle the boiling broth over. Serve with extra chilli and lime wedges.

items.symptom: Broth lacks depth or tastes flat
items.cause: Not enough simmering time or insufficient aromatics
items.fix: Bun bo Hue needs at least 2 hours of simmering to develop. Make sure the lemongrass is well bruised and the shallots are properly charred. Shrimp paste adds umami depth -- even a small amount transforms the broth.

content.text: Bun bo Hue is the pride of the central Vietnamese city of Hue. The imperial court cuisine of Hue is famous for its complexity and refinement. This soup reflects that heritage. It is bolder and more aromatic than pho. In Vietnam it is eaten for breakfast. The bright orange colour comes from the chilli oil and annatto.
